newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU ministers to resume euro pact talks tonight.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to resume euro pact talks tonight.

text.p: European Union finance ministers will resume talks on Thursday evening aimed at securing agreement over fiscal discipline to protect a future single European currency, EU sources said.

The talks had earlier broken up and it had not been clear whether they would resume this evening or whether the ministers would hand over a decision about the terms of the stability pact to a summit of EU leaders starting in Dublin on Friday.
"They will definitely go back to it later," the EU source said of the debate on the stability pact.

Under the pact, championed by Germany, countries running a deficit of more than three percent of national output under the EU's planned monetary union would be fined unless they wre suffering a serious economic recession.
The dispute is over what the definition of a recession should be. Germany has been isolated in holding out for a strict definition.
The EU intends to launch monetary union on January 1, 1999.
